scope: Analytic sphere/torus surface-surface intersection in the axial configuration (ninth analytic SS slice, one cell): native intersect_sphere_torus in crates/brep-core/src/intersections/sphere_torus.rs, bridge op brep_intersect_sphere_torus, typed TS adapter intersectSphereTorus. The cell reuses both existing recognizers unchanged (sphere_sphere::recognize for the canonical stereographic sphere, plane_torus::recognize_torus for the exact sixteen-patch strict ring-torus solid with tensor-product weights [[1,w,1],[w,w^2,w],[1,w,1]], w = cos(pi/4), rigid affine placements admitted); plane_torus.rs changes are visibility-only (torus_residual and lift_parallel promoted to pub(crate)). The sphere operand is always first — swapped order is an explicit unsupported_surface region. Axiality is certified, never forced: a perpendicular offset of the sphere center at pure rounding scale (64 binary64 epsilons of the axial/radius terms) snaps to the torus axis, an offset inside the recognition-scale band (1e-9 of the radius sum) reports near_coincidence, and a clearly off-axis pair is unsupported_surface (the general sphere/torus pair is a quartic, out of scope — no numerical fallback). Both surfaces are surfaces of revolution about the shared axis, so the section reduces to circle/circle in the meridian half-plane (rho >= 0, z): the torus side (rho - R)^2 + z^2 = r_t^2 against the sphere rho^2 + (z - h)^2 = r_s^2 with h the sphere center height above the torus center plane. Classification uses outward binary64 bands widened by both recognition deviations: provably separate (d > r_t + r_s + band) or provably contained (d + band < |r_t - r_s|) meridian circles resolve empty by the interval signs; the meridian tangencies (double roots, d == r_t + r_s externally or d == |r_t - r_s| internally) stay tangency_or_multiple_root — the tangent contact revolves into a circle but is never a guessed circle; a root whose revolved radius collapses into the band degenerates to a pole point on the axis and stays unresolved (unreachable for a canonical strict ring torus, whose roots keep rho >= R - r_t >= 1e-5 — kept as an honest guard, never guessed through). For a strict ring torus every meridian root sits on the torus meridian circle, whose rho is clearly positive, so both roots always revolve: resolved configurations are exactly the two-circle family (a one-circle configuration would require rho* <= 0, i.e. a horn/spindle torus refused at construction). Resolved contacts are exact rational circles (four 90-degree arcs, weights cos(pi/4), knots 0..=4) with UV lifts on both surfaces: on the torus, iso-v parallels at the exact profile angle phi = atan2(z*, rho* - R) mapped through the exact rational 90-degree-arc parameter map t = s/(1+s), s = sqrt(2) tan(phi/2)/(1 - tan(phi/2)) — one degree-1 line per revolution quadrant patch of the profile row; on the sphere, the per-patch stereographic UV circles/lines of sphere_sphere::lift. There is no sphere/torus surface coincidence, so coincident_trim does not arise. Nothing here authorizes a topology change (permitsTopologyChange stays false).

limitations: Canonical operands only: the sphere is the exact canonical stereographic sphere solid; the torus is the exact canonical strict ring-torus solid (R - r >= 1e-5; horn and spindle tori are refused at construction); everything else is an explicit unsupported_surface region, never a numerical fallback

Axial configuration only: the sphere center must be certified on the torus axis; clearly off-axis pairs are honest unsupported_surface regions (the general sphere/torus pair is a quartic) with a near_coincidence band at recognition scale, never forced axial

Resolved sections are exactly the two-circle family: for a strict ring torus both meridian roots revolve (a one-circle configuration would require a horn/spindle torus); the meridian tangencies (double roots at both equators and off-center) stay tangency_or_multiple_root, and the pole-collapse guard is unreachable-but-honest — tangent contacts are never guessed circles or points
coincident_trim is deliberately unused: a sphere can never coincide with a curved torus patch

NumericallyResolved is not certified complete-domain coverage and permitsTopologyChange stays false; consuming these sections in Booleans and the remaining analytic SS pairs (torus/torus, cylinder/torus, cone/torus) stay open
